title: Highest IQ score, Roosevelt brain trust and Eleanor Roosevelt
summary: Rose says his top college IQ score brought him to Washington under the Roosevelt brain trust. He befriended Eleanor Roosevelt and was sent to interview Einstein and Dewey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Well, I remember it for quite a while. It didn't start until 1946. Oh, I see. But I had an interest in it because of my own early career, which had to do with the fact that I had the highest IQ score in the nation on the original college... When they first instituted the college IQ testing for a freshman the first year, I had the highest IQ in the nation. And the Roosevelt administration, at that time, through its brain trust with Raymond Moley and Rexford Guy Tugwell, came up with this crackpot program of picking out the most intelligent kids and bringing them to Washington and doing a big thing. So I got to know the president, Mrs. Roosevelt, and I became close friends with Eleanor Roosevelt and spent a lot of time with her in my early days. And I had the opportunity to meet people that I wanted to discuss certain things with. And the government made it possible for me to interview Albert Einstein and John Dewey. And this is how I met Rivera, too.
Mm-hmm. That's how you met Rivera.
